items.title: Saltwater flooding could radically change which crops are worth growing
items.summary: Saltwater isn't something most people associate with English farmland. But in parts of eastern England, it's becoming a growing problem, not just for crops but for farm incomes too.

items.title: Gravitational-wave analysis narrows the search for black hole impostors
items.summary: Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. When two black holes orbit each other and merge, they produce gravitational waves (i.e., ripples in spacetime) that can resemble those emitted by mergers involving other exotic compact objects.

items.title: Fish may be highly sensitive to antidepressants found in water
items.summary: Many of the drugs that target human brain chemistry, such as antidepressants, are still biologically active when they leave the body. These substances and their metabolites can persist in wastewater and eventually end up in the sea, rivers or other aquatic environments.

items.title: Cataract surgery will be needed in space, surgeon predicts
items.summary: An eye surgeon with a passion for space since childhood predicts that as astronauts start to make journeys to the moon and Mars in the near future, eye surgery in space will eventually become a necessity.

items.title: NASA's next great observatory could spot oceans on distant worlds
items.summary: We've found more than 5,500 exoplanets so far. Dozens of them are in the habitable zones of their parent stars, where, at least in theory, they could host an ocean. But we've never definitively found a liquid ocean on another planet.

items.summary: Most men may be missing an important dietary clue about prostate cancer. items.title: Scientists are building a microscope powered by a quantum computer
items.summary: Scientists are combining an electron microscope with a quantum computer to squeeze far more information from each electron. The approach could reveal faint details with fewer electrons, helping protect fragile samples that conventional microscopy can damage.

items.title: Researchers pinpoint key early-universe measurement with record precision
items.summary: An international team, including researchers from the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, has reached a major milestone in "precision cosmology" by measuring the amount of helium created in the universe's first five minutes with unprecedented accuracy.

items.summary: Long before dinosaurs appeared on Earth, fierce predatory fish developed crushing jaws and sharp teeth to survive and diversify in ancient oceans.
